readback.name: Poincare.BufferedTensorGraphTransport.exists_destination_Y_entry_transport
readback.mathematical_statement: For arbitrary universe u and topological M with EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) charts and a C∞ manifold structure for the boundaryless model 𝓡 3, let A be AtlasData. This packages a finite family of extended charts whose sources cover M, open regions covering M whose closures lie in the corresponding chart sources and have compact coordinate images, and a smooth partition of unity on all M subordinate to those regions. No separate T2Space, CompactSpace, ConnectedSpace, or symmetry of the input entries is a binder in this declaration. Fix chart indices i,j, output tensor indices c,d : Fin 3, and total maps θ,ξ : E → ℝ and F : E → E. The destination is chart i, the source is chart j, and change(i,j)(z) = chart j((chart i)⁻¹(z)). Assume θ is C∞ and compactly supported, ξ is C∞, and F is C∞ and compactly supported. Assume tsupport θ lies in the genuine source of the partial transition (chart i)⁻¹.trans(chart j); for every z in tsupport θ, F equals change(i,j) eventually near z; and θ(z)=1 on the set chart i '' (tsupport(partition i) ∩ (chart j)⁻¹ '' tsupport ξ). θ is not required to be nonnegative or bounded by 1; ξ need not have compact support; F is not assumed to be a global diffeomorphism. For every real 0<α<1 there exists a nonnegative constant C, chosen before the real time horizon T, such that for every T there is a continuous real linear map Q from the ordinary finite product of nine Scalar(α,T) carriers indexed by (a,b) : Fin 3 × Fin 3 to one Scalar(α,T), with operator norm at most C. Scalar(α,T) is the concrete parabolic Hölder carrier of bounded scalar functions on [0,T] × E, extended by zero at all other times, with bounded scaled differences for distance ‖x-y‖ + sqrt(|t-s|) and norm sup norm plus α-Hölder seminorm; the domain finite product uses its ordinary supremum norm. For every input w and every p=(t,z), Q(w)(p) = Σₐᵦ weight(i,θ,ξ,F,a,b,c,d)(z) w(a,b)(t,F(z)), where weight(z) = θ(z) partition i((chart i)⁻¹(z)) ξ(F(z)) (DF(z)e_c)_a (DF(z)e_d)_b. It vanishes at every time outside coordSupport(A,i) = chart i '' tsupport(partition i). For every x in chart i.source and every real t, its genuine-chart evaluation equals partition i(x) times an if-expression: when x is in chart j.source it is Σₐᵦ ξ(chart j(x)) jac(i,j,x,a,c) jac(i,j,x,b,d) w(a,b)(t,chart j(x)); otherwise it is zero. Here jac(i,j,x,a,c) is the a-coordinate of Dchange(i,j)(chart i(x)) applied to e_c. The formula has the destination partition factor partition i exactly once and the source coordinate multiplier ξ exactly once. It has no partition j factor: arbitrary source entries w are inputs, and this theorem does not require or certify that they already carry a source partition. Q depends on T but its bound C does not; for T<0 the cylinder is empty and the carrier is zero, while the statement still quantifies over all real T. The conclusion constructs one destination entry in the actual Y carrier, not a global compatible tensor, not an X graph with derivative equations, and not chart overlap compatibility or symmetry. The input local agreement F=change is a real localization assumption rather than an assumption of the requested Q or its boundedness.
